message.content:
Search this repository for webhook dispatching related to memo lifecycle events. I need to find:
1. Which memo events (create, update, delete, etc.) trigger webhook dispatches
2. The function names that dispatch these webhooks
3. Where all webhook dispatches converge for actual delivery (the common delivery function/path)

Search broadly — look for "webhook" combined with "memo", "dispatch", "DispatchMemo", etc. Check Go files, TypeScript files, and any other relevant code. Search breadth: very thorough.

Look in directories like server/, plugin/, store/, api/, and similar. Check for function names like "DispatchMemoCreated", "dispatchMemoWebhook", etc. Also look for a common webhook dispatch or post/send function that all events funnel through.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## Webhook Dispatching for Memo Lifecycle Events

### 1. Memo Events That Trigger Webhook Dispatches

There are exactly **four** memo-related activity types that trigger webhooks:

| Activity Type String | Lifecycle Event | Trigger Location |
|---|---|---|
| `memos.memo.created` | Memo is created | `CreateMemo` in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (line 157) |
| `memos.memo.updated` | Memo is updated | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go` (line 67) |
| `memos.memo.deleted` | Memo is deleted | `DeleteMemo` in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (line 562) |
| `memos.memo.comment.created` | Comment is created on a memo | `CreateMemoComment` in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` (line 119) |

The `memos.memo.updated` event is dispatched through the helper `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`, which is called from three places:
- `UpdateMemo` in `memo_service.go` (line 513)
- `SetMemoAttachments` in `memo_attachment_service.go` (line 48)
- `SetMemoRelations` in `memo_relation_service.go` (line 48)

### 2. Function Names That Dispatch These Webhooks

All defined in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`:

- **`DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook`** (line 15) -- delegates to `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` with activity type `"memos.memo.created"`
- **`DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook`** (line 20) -- delegates to `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` with activity type `"memos.memo.updated"`
- **`DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook`** (line 25) -- delegates to `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` with activity type `"memos.memo.deleted"`
- **`DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook`** (line 30) -- handles comment webhooks directly (sends to the *related memo creator's* webhooks, not the comment author's), with activity type `"memos.memo.comment.created"`

There is also a private shared helper:
- **`dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`** (line 48) -- shared by the first three functions. It resolves the memo creator, fetches that user's webhooks via `s.Store.GetUserWebhooks(ctx, creatorID)`, builds a payload for each, and calls `webhook.PostAsync(payload)`.

And a convenience wrapper in `memo_update_helpers.go`:
- **`dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`** (line 66) -- calls `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` and also broadcasts an SSE event.

### 3. Common Delivery Path (Where All Dispatches Converge)

All four webhook dispatch functions converge on the same delivery infrastructure in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`:

**`webhook.PostAsync(payload)`** (line 184) -- Every webhook dispatch in the codebase calls this function. It is the sole entry point. There are exactly two call sites, both in `memo_service_webhooks.go` (lines 43 and 71):
- Line 43: inside `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook`
- Line 71: inside `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (used by created/updated/deleted)

`PostAsync` enqueues the `*WebhookRequestPayload` onto a buffered channel (`asyncPostQueue`, capacity 128). If the queue is full, the payload is dropped with a warning log.

**`webhook.Post(payload)`** (line 120) -- The synchronous delivery function. Four goroutines (spawned in `init()`, line 42-55) consume from `asyncPostQueue` and call `Post` for each payload. This function:
1. JSON-marshals the payload
2. Creates an HTTP POST request with `Content-Type: application/json`
3. If a `SigningSecret` is set, computes an HMAC-SHA256 signature following the Standard Webhooks spec and sets `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` headers
4. Sends the request using `safeClient` (an `http.Client` with a 30-second timeout and SSRF-safe dialer that blocks reserved/private IP ranges)
5. Reads the response and checks for a successful status code

### Summary of the Full Call Chain

```
CreateMemo ──────────────────> DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook ──┐
                                                            │
UpdateMemo ──┐                                              ├──> dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook ──> webhook.PostAsync ──┐
SetMemoAttachments ──┤──> dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects    │                                                       │
SetMemoRelations ────┘    └──> DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook ──┘                                                       │
                                                                                                                    ├──> [async queue] ──> webhook.Post (HTTP POST)
DeleteMemo ──────────────────> DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook ──> dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook ──> webhook.PostAsync ──────┘
                                                                                                                    │
CreateMemoComment ───────────> DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook ──────────────────────────> webhook.PostAsync ──────┘
```

### Key Files

- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` -- All four `DispatchMemo*Webhook` functions and the shared `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` helper
- `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go` -- `PostAsync` (async enqueue), `Post` (HTTP delivery), `WebhookRequestPayload` struct, signing logic, SSRF-safe HTTP client
- `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go` -- URL and signing secret validation, SSRF IP range blocking
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` -- Call sites for `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` (line 157) and `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` (line 562)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go` -- `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` calling `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (line 67)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` -- Call site for `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (line 119)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go` -- Calls `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (line 48)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go` -- Calls `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (line 48)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go` -- CRUD operations for user webhook configuration (not dispatching)
- `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` -- `GetUserWebhooks`, `AddUserWebhook`, `RemoveUserWebhook`, `UpdateUserWebhook` (store-layer persistence)
